Author: Hardy, Steve
Title: Here's how technology helped save Baton Rouge in summer of crisis
Abstract Note: Warren Kron stood in front of a map of East Baton Rouge splattered in green. Each dot represents a person who had called for rescue during the August flood.
Extra: During the flood, IT workers mapped 911 calls in real time to help the fire department direct rescue boats, said Kron, the city-parish's GIS manager. Afterward, the local government extrapolated from the 911 calls — and subsequent 311 calls — to form a rough estimate of the damage area. It was important to get that information out because the state was going to need federal assistance to rebuild, and the maps laid bare the extent of the flooding, Kron explained.

Author: Hardy, Steve
Title: Baton Rouge wins praise for new website, online data tools
Abstract Note: Baton Rouge's city-parish web presence has won recognition from a national technology research organization.
Extra: East Baton Rouge has also continued to divulge city-parish government records through its Open Data portal the mayor's office noted in a Wednesday news release. Other projects have included improvements to the city-parish 311 app, new digital blight-fighting tools, additional information on local government contracts and data that tracks and maps local conditions, such as current the current traffic.

Author: Gallo, Andrea
Title: Data on tax assessments, flood losses for every East Baton Rouge property
Abstract Note: It's a question most people wonder but are too polite to ask: How much are your neighbors paying in property taxes, and how much money are their homes worth?
Extra: The city-parish released a data set Monday through its Open Data BR website, data.brla.gov, that allows people to scroll through tax roll assessments for every piece of property in East Baton Rouge Parish, answering those questions without awkward conversations. Not only does the data set show fair market and assessed values, it also reveals new insight into how much property damage the August floods caused. The 2016 property tax data includes reassessed values that the Assessor's Office recalculated after August floods ruined homes and took hundreds of thousands of dollars off the bottom lines of property values. https://data.brla.gov/Housing-and-Development/EBRP-Tax-Roll/myfc-nh6n/data

Author: Wallace, Ben
Title: New EBR website provides public access to data on crime, employee salaries and more
Abstract Note: Finding out where crimes and fires occur in Baton Rouge just became much easier thanks to a new website the city-parish unveiled on Friday.
Extra: The website, “Open Data BR,” features loads of information about everything from the locations of crimes and car crashes to the salaries of city-parish employees. Anyone with Internet access can view the information for free at https://data.brla.gov.

Author: Hardy, Steve
Title: East Baton Rouge officials inviting public to submit more open records requests
Abstract Note: Flipping the script, East Baton Rouge officials are asking residents to request government records so more documents can see the light of day.
Extra: The city-parish's Information Technology department operates the Open Data website at http://data.brla.gov/.

Author: Hardy, Steve
Title: East Baton Rouge releases municipal checkbook information to public
Abstract Note: Baton Rougeans can now track how the local government is spending public tax dollars, as the city-parish has decided to put its checkbook information online.
Extra: The new site is checkbook.brla.gov, and a spreadsheet is available at data.brla.gov/Government/Open-Checkbook-BR/7qhq-wwsg/data. The report is available at brla.gov/opendatareport. City-parish data, including employee salaries, city-parish contracts, property tax information and various interactive maps are available at data.brla.gov and gis.brla.gov.

Author: Wilkins, James
Title: Baton Rouge developing City-Parish Chatbot to help improve website experience using AI
Abstract Note: Baton Rouge officials are working to develop an artificial intelligence chatbot designed to act as a virtual assistant, allowing residents and visitors to more quickly find answers to questions about

Author: Morris, George
Title: Community: Civic associations learn about East Baton Rouge city-parish digital media
Extra: Eric Romero, director of information services, and Warren Kron, manager of geographic information services, explained how the city's website, brla.gov, has been replaced and the GIS platform expanded. Author: Hardy, Steve
Title: Interactive: See just how high floodwaters rose across East Baton Rouge
Abstract Note: A new map shows just how high the waters rose during last summer's flood.
Extra: The new data is based on high water mark surveys taken by the U.S. Geological Survey and the Amite River Basin Commission. City-parish senior geographic information system analyst Brandon Jumonville then combined those findings with existing elevation and watershed maps to determine the maximum water depth during the flood, GIS manager Warren Kron said.  The new map also compared the scientific model to the rough and ready version produced days after the storm by looking at aerial photos, 911 calls and Facebook posts from residents pointing out flooded areas. There are some disparities between the two, but overall Kron said the new map validates the earlier effort. The newest map is the final entry on the city-parish's flood story data set at http://ebrgis.maps.arcgis.com/apps/MapSeries/index.html?appid=1c4ac9fca97846d2a1780a90fc68c6eb. The full, technical version with all the layers and metadata is available at http://ebrgis.maps.arcgis.com/home/webmap/viewer.html?webmap=c67e95809261466595dcbf5860d6a29a.

Author: Nicholson, Lara
Title: Officials seek crime prevention districts to revitalize North Baton Rouge neighborhoods
Abstract Note: Neighborhood residents will have to vote on whether to impose property taxes for their districts.
Extra: There are at least 30 crime prevention districts in East Baton Rouge Parish spanning from Shenandoah Estates to Live Oak Trace in Zachary, according to city-parish data. https://gisdata.brla.gov/datasets/a51dd9b85ee44e88b9a777f0e925e867/explore?showTable=true

Author: Hardy, Steve
Title: Baton Rouge's public information website offers resources for citizen watchdogs
Abstract Note: New crime statistics, property maps and government financial reports could soon give East Baton Rouge watchdogs a more complete view of the community's workings.
Extra: Several weeks ago, city-parish staff asked residents to request records that the local government could publish on its public information website, http://data.brla.gov/, or its mapping website, http://gis.brla.gov/.

Author: Hardy, Steve
Title: East Baton Rouge government makes more information available to public through online sites and apps
Abstract Note: Amidst a push to make data more available to the public, East Baton Rouge Parish residents can now find expanded voting and land records online.
Extra: The parish has combined data from the Louisiana Secretary of State’s office with its own online maps to allow users to view precinct-by-precinct election breakdowns. http://ebrgis.maps.arcgis.com/apps/webappviewer/index.html?id=bffcd9c0aeea40f9853993c6dc4956c0 The information services department also touched on a few other recent projects aimed at streamlining government services — such as partnering with Google’s traffic app Waze and developing real-time 911 tracking for police — and on efforts to make more information available to the public online, such as tax rolls and other items at Open Data BR and the city-parish’s annual budget. http://budget.brla.gov/#!/year/default

Author: Hardy, Steve
Title: Video: New technology tracks crime, traffic reports in real time, to help Baton Rouge police coordinate response
Abstract Note: Police, reporters and city officials huddled around a screen as dots and symbols appeared over a digital map of Baton Rouge representing officers’ movement and reports of crime and traffic
Extra: The result is a bird’s eye view of Baton Rouge that updates with every traffic jam, 911 call and weather event. Police said the new technology will help supervisors better direct their officers on the ground and marshal resources during a disaster.

Author: Triggs, Ariana
Title: Mayor Broome announces launch of Open Neighborhood BR platform
Abstract Note: Open Neighborhood BR, a new digital resource for residents, is now live, Mayor-President Sharon Weston Broome announced today. The platform, located at my.brla.gov, is focused on providing resident…
Extra: The Open Neighborhood BR platform is a first of its kind resource, leveraging public datasets available through the Open Data BR portal – along with geographic information systems (GIS) map layers available through the eBRGIS program – to provide unprecedented insights into neighborhood-level activity through searchable map views and custom date ranges involving recent incidents or requests for service surrounding a specific address or street. http://my.brla.gov

Author: Shueh, Jason
Title: Baton Rouge Mayor Talks Open Data Portal Launch
Abstract Note: What does it really take to launch an open data portal for the first time?
Extra: In Louisiana's city of Baton Rouge and East Baton Rouge Parish, open data isn’t just a technical solution. Rather, it’s viewed as a catalyst for transparency and economic growth, and as a connection point between the city and its citizens. http://data.brla.gov/

Author: Allen, Rebekah
Title: City-parish website offers window into parish government spending
Abstract Note: Do you want to know where and how your tax dollars are being spent in East Baton Rouge Parish?
Extra: Mayor-President Kip Holden announced the launch of “Open Budget BR” today, a website that breaks down city-parish spending and allows people to drill down into department, program, construction and service spending and funding. http://budget.brla.gov/#!/year/default
